New services must use **`gateway-api`**. The deciding file is [`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r3000/policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml) in `dshnayder-org/infra` @ `git-access-ab/r3000` (commit `d8093b1`).

## Exact text

From `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`, verbatim:

```
# policy: ingress-class
# version: v3   effective: 2026-04-19   status: current
# subject: which ingress implementation new services must use
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1
kind: FleetPolicy
metadata:
  name: ingress-class-v3
spec:
  effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19
  status: current
  setting: gateway-api
```

## Why v3 and not the others

`policy/ingress-class/` holds three versions; only v3 is `status: current`.

| File | `setting` | `status` | `effectiveFrom` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy/ingress-class/v1.yaml` | `nginx` | `superseded` | `2024-03-11` |
| `policy/ingress-class/v2.yaml` | `gce-ingress` | `superseded` | `2025-06-02` |
| `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` | `gateway-api` | `current` | `2026-04-19` |

v1 (`nginx`) is marked `# status: superseded by v2` and v2 (`gce-ingress`) `# status: superseded by v3`, so both are historical.

## Coverage of the search

The repo has no `docs/standards`, no ADRs, and no OPA/Gatekeeper/Kyverno rules or CI checks — `docs/` contains only a generated fleet inventory and one Russian-language recovery runbook. A case-insensitive scan of every tracked file for `ingress`, `ingressclass`, `gateway-api` and `nginx` matches **only** the three files above; nothing under `clusters/` (468 clusters), `services/`, `modules/`, `scripts/` or `vendor/` references an ingress implementation. So `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` is the sole mandate, and it is prose-free policy-as-data rather than a written standard.

## Answer

`maxSurge` is `0` on the `batch` pool of `prod-us-central1` because surging above zero double-books the pool's reserved TPU quota during an upgrade, so the pool fails to come back. The rationale exists **only in git history** — there is no comment, doc, or ADR in the repo that says it.

The stated reason, verbatim from the commit message of [`d10fd3d`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/d10fd3d016c6af4c0ccbe5ab145257f0f960686c) (`fix(clusters): pin maxSurge to 0`, 2026-02-01, Meridian Platform):

> maxSurge above zero double-books the reserved TPU quota during an upgrade and the whole pool fails to come back; see INC-2219.

That commit changed the value from a placeholder:

```diff
-  maxSurge: PLACEHOLDER
+  maxSurge: 0
```

## The value in the repo

[`clusters/prod-us-central1/nodepool-batch.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/d10fd3d016c6af4c0ccbe5ab145257f0f960686c/clusters/prod-us-central1/nodepool-batch.yaml) in full, verbatim:

```yaml
# nodepool-batch
apiVersion: meridian.io/v1
kind: Setting
spec:
  maxSurge: 0
```

The other two pools on the same cluster both use `maxSurge: 1` — `clusters/prod-us-central1/nodepool-general.yaml` and `clusters/prod-us-central1/nodepool-gpu.yaml`. Across the whole repo this is the only `maxSurge: 0`; every other cluster's pools sit at `1`–`3`.

- **No PR.** `d10fd3d` is a direct commit with no merge commit or PR reference attached.

That file is shaped unlike its siblings: `kind: Setting` under `apiVersion: meridian.io/v1`, with no `metadata.name` and no `spec.cluster`, whereas `nodepool-general.yaml` and `nodepool-gpu.yaml` are `kind: NodePool` under `container.meridian.io/v1`. It is still listed in `clusters/prod-us-central1/kustomization.yaml`, so as written it may not bind to the `batch` pool at all.

## Answer

`reconcileNodePool` is defined **twice** on `dshnayder-org/infra` @ `git-access-ab/r3000` (HEAD `d8093b1`). **The branch does not contain the evidence needed to prove which copy the controller compiles** — there is no `go.mod`, no `go.work`, no `main` package, no Makefile/Dockerfile, and no CI workflow anywhere in the tree, so there is no import graph, no replace directive and no build invocation to resolve. The only statement on the subject is a code comment, which is a claim, not proof.

## The two implementations

| File | Package | Signature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`modules/controller/nodepool.go:5`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r3000/modules/controller/nodepool.go) | `controller` | `func reconcileNodePool(ctx context.Context, pool *Pool) error` |
| [`vendor/upstream-operator/nodepool.go:5`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r3000/vendor/upstream-operator/nodepool.go) | `upstream` | `func reconcileNodePool(ctx context.Context, pool *Pool) error` |

Both are **package-level functions with no receiver type** — neither is a method. Same signature; they differ only in the tag they pass through: `"first-party"` vs `"vendored"`.

## What the branch does and does not prove

- The only claim of exclusion is a comment, `vendor/upstream-operator/nodepool.go:3-4`: `// reconcileNodePool is vendored from upstream-operator v0.14.2. Do not edit;` / `// this copy is not compiled into the controller.` The counterpart comment at `modules/controller/nodepool.go:3` says only `// reconcileNodePool is the first-party implementation.`
- **No build tags exist anywhere.** `git grep -n -E '^//(go:build| \+build)' -- '*.go'` returns nothing. No `_test.go` and no GOOS/GOARCH suffixes either.
- **No Go module exists.** The whole branch contains exactly four `.go` files: the two above plus `modules/controller/quota.go` and `vendor/upstream-operator/quota.go`. There is no `go.mod`, so there is no module path and no `replace` directive to point at either copy.
- **Neither file could compile as written.** Both use `context.Context` and `*Pool` and call `reconcile(...)`, and no file on the branch imports `context` or defines `Pool` or `reconcile`. This is a manifest tree with four illustrative Go stubs in it, not a buildable controller.

## Answer

Yes — `clusters/prod-us-central1/policy-base.yaml` is a **symlink**, not a regular file. Its target string is exactly:

```
../../policy/base.yaml
```

Relative to `clusters/prod-us-central1/`, that resolves to `policy/base.yaml` at the repo root, which **exists** as a regular file.

## Evidence

Repo [dshnayder-org/infra](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra), branch `git-access-ab/r3000`, commit `d8093b1becb8aa5f0ec9b0d9424d96c826676f08`.

- `git ls-files -s clusters/prod-us-central1/policy-base.yaml` → `120000 11eb2b917b754456c3005c9524cff86e963a59c7 0` — mode `120000` is a symlink.
- `ls -l` shows `policy-base.yaml -> ../../policy/base.yaml`; the blob's contents (the link target string) are `../../policy/base.yaml`.
- It is the only symlink tracked on this branch.

Contents of the target, quoted verbatim from `policy/base.yaml` (mode `100644`, blob `3f1ad56871beb6e12b6ae39dd385a42427c834fa`):

```yaml
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1

  inherit: true
```

## Evidence

Both commands were run in a checkout of [dshnayder-org/infra](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra) at branch `git-access-ab/r3000`, commit `d8093b1becb8aa5f0ec9b0d9424d96c826676f08`:

- `git ls-tree git-access-ab/r3000 -- scripts/rotate-keys.sh` →
  `100755 blob f9829bbba1abbf48558fd4cc88931916132a64c7	scripts/rotate-keys.sh`
- `git ls-files -s scripts/rotate-keys.sh` →
  `100755 f9829bbba1abbf48558fd4cc88931916132a64c7 0	scripts/rotate-keys.sh`

The two agree on both mode and blob id. `100755` = regular executable (not `100644` non-executable, not `120000` symlink). The checked-out file matches: `-rwxr-xr-x` with `core.fileMode=true`.

## Path check

A case-insensitive scan of the whole tree (`git ls-tree -r --full-tree | grep -i 'rotate.keys'`) returns exactly one path — `scripts/rotate-keys.sh` — so there is no variant under a different path or casing. `scripts/` on this branch contains only that one file.

Worth noting: the script's own header comment states it is invoked directly by `.github/workflows/rotate.yml` rather than via `bash`, so the executable bit is load-bearing and must not be dropped.
